explanation: The V82A mutation reduces the S1/S1′ subpocket volume by over 50 Ų through loss of the valine's branched methyl groups, creating a hydrophobic cavity that no longer optimally accommodates lopinavir's bulky inhibitor scaffold at the 3.3 Å contact interface. This volumetric shrinkage forces lopinavir into a suboptimal binding geometry, disrupting favorable van der Waals interactions that normally stabilize the inhibitor within this critical binding pocket and destabilizing the enzyme-inhibitor complex. The decreased hydrophobicity further weakens the hydrophobic contacts that anchor lopinavir, collectively reducing binding affinity despite the mutation occurring at the periphery of the active site (10.3 Å from ligand center).
